extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newspaper editors, Associated Press members, and general news readers
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting of Associated Press board policy and resolutions regarding provision of AP news to governments, the risks of government broadcasting as propaganda, contractual limits on use, and the agency's commitment to objectivity and free news exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to freedom of the press and international news exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Associated Press stands committed to the principle of freedom of press and freedom of international news exchange... It holds that news disseminated by non-governmental news agencies is essential to the highest development of mankind and the perpetuation of peace between nations.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames AP's mission: non-governmental dissemination and free flow of news are core values. Used as justification for resisting government-controlled newscasting and for preserving independent reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectivity of Associated Press reports
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Associated Press report should be objective ... The acceptibility of the report as objective is the problem of The [Associated Press].”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AP must ensure reports are presented objectively. The board recognizes that whether a report is deemed objective is a key responsibility of the organization; objectivity is the standard by which AP reports are judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition against furnishing news to any government for propaganda purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: “The AP has no commitment to furnish its news to any government for propaganda purposes.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AP policy is not to supply material for government propaganda. This is an explicit boundary: supplying news for overt government propaganda is disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit use to domestic broadcasts within government borders (not international propaganda)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The AP does furnish news to broadcasting departments of other governments but 'it does so solely for domestic broadcast and not for international propaganda purposes.'”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When AP supplies government broadcasting services, the intended use must be domestic-only within that government’s borders; international dissemination by a government would be disallowed as it risks becoming propaganda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renegotiate contracts to restrict international use of AP material
rubrics_metrics.description: “The adoption of the resolution included instruction to renegotiate all contracts which were in process ... to provide only for the domestic use within their own borders of Associated Press news. Other contracts, including the one with Tass, already call for such limited use.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational requirement: actively seek contractual clauses that limit government partners to domestic use of AP content; review and amend existing agreements accordingly (e.g., Tass and others).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of government newscasting because it creates fear of propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: “We hold, however, that Government cannot engage in newscasting without creating the fear of propaganda which necessarily would reflect upon the objectivity of the news services.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principle: government involvement in newscasting—even if well-intentioned—undermines perceived objectivity. AP should therefore avoid arrangements that could create such perceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition that broadcasts designed to promote a viewpoint are propaganda (even if 'good' from one perspective)
rubrics_metrics.description: “We hold that any broadcast designed to promote ... will of necessity be propaganda—good propaganda, possibly, from an American viewpoint ... but certainly not objective presentation.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on content evaluation: material aimed to promote a national/political viewpoint is to be treated as propaganda and not as objective news, regardless of alignment with AP’s values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain non-governmental dissemination as a contribution to international understanding and peace
rubrics_metrics.description: “...news dissemination by non-governmental news agencies is essential ... and makes its contribution to universal understanding.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value statement used to justify policies that favor independent agency-to-agency news exchange rather than state-directed dissemination; suggests prioritizing independent distribution channels to foster peace and understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance action: terminate or modify services conflicting with principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The board adopted resolutions (including instruction to terminate certain services and to renegotiate contracts) when such services conflict with AP principles about propaganda and objective reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical standard: the board will take governance actions—including termination or by-law amendments—to ensure organizational practice aligns with stated principles about objectivity and non-propaganda use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of financial and legal consequences in policy decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The board noted the three-year cost to the AP of the Government's antitrust suit (including fees and expenses) and that expenses have increased materially; these financial realities were cited in discussing organizational decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While chiefly normative, the policy-making process also weighs financial/legal impacts (litigation costs, revenue shortfalls) when deciding on services, contract negotiations, or structural changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary limitations/exceptions pending internal reform (by-laws and membership considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The court temporarily enjoined the exclusive right of The Associated Press to the news of its members until the AP amended by-laws to address competitive factors in election of members; the board appointed committees and held special meetings to conform by-laws with decrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational rubric: when judicial or external constraints arise, AP will pursue internal governance reforms (by-law amendments, committee reviews, special meetings) to address competitive/organizational issues while preserving core principles.
